- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk aversion fading.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >10% from prior period) and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in next forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day prior true value if sentiment is stable or mildly bullish.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.33), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before applying correction.
